exercise.name: Fire Hydrant

reference.title: Bent Leg Side Kick (kneeling) (male)
reference.listing: Video; data sheet: body part Hips, equipment Body weight, exercise type Strength

exercise.mechanics: Isolation (hip abduction in flexion, knee bent)

breathing.pattern: Exhale as the knee lifts out, inhale as it lowers.
breathing.cadence: About 1.2 s up, 0.6 s hold, 1.6 s down

prescription.progression: Pause at the top, then a mini band above the knees, then an ankle weight

cues.text: On all fours: hands under the shoulders, knees under the hips, back flat, neck long.
Breathe out and lift the bent right knee out to the side, shin level with the floor.
Pause at the top; trunk still, weight evenly on both hands.
Breathe in and lower the knee back under the hip with control.
Knee just touches the mat; repeat, then switch legs.

mistakes.mistake: Leaning the trunk away to lift the knee higher
mistakes.fix: Keep the shoulders and hips level; lift only as high as the hip allows.
Keep the shin level, knee bent 90 degrees.
Lift in about a second, pause, lower slower.

kinematics.norm: Hands under the shoulders, knees under the hips (clinical opinion)
Thigh lifts out to the side as far as the hip allows without trunk lean (clinical opinion); the rig caps hip abduction at 45 degrees
About 1 s up, a short pause, 1.5-2 s down (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #303512, Bent Leg Side Kick (kneeling) (male), video (movement reference)

Selkowitz, Beneck & Powers 2013, which exercises target the gluteal muscles while minimizing activation of the tensor fascia lata? Fine-wire EMG of 11 exercises (J Orthop Sports Phys Ther 43(2):54-64)
Macadam, Cronin & Contreras 2015, gluteal muscle activity in dynamic hip abduction and hip external rotation exercise: a systematic review (Int J Sports Phys Ther 10(5):573-591; PMC4595911)
Boren et al. 2011, EMG analysis of gluteus medius and gluteus maximus during rehabilitation exercises (Int J Sports Phys Ther 6(3):206-223; PMC3201064)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, numbness or cramping occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
Use a mat or folded towel under the knees.
modify: Wrist discomfort: fists or forearms on the mat.
Groin or hip pinch: lift less high.

muscleNotes.glute_med_r: Abducts the bent leg out to the side with the hip flexed. No EMG study of the quadruped version was found; the closest is the clam (abduction and external rotation with the hips flexed), which reached about 27% MVIC gluteus medius and 44% superior gluteus maximus with low TFL (Selkowitz 2013).
muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Upper fibres assist abduction and external rotation in flexion (Selkowitz 2013 clam data; applying it here is clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.glute_med_l: Support side: keeps the pelvis level (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.core: Stops the trunk leaning away from the lifting leg (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.obliques_r: Resist the trunk side-bending and rotating (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.obliques_l: Resist the trunk side-bending and rotating (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.serratus_r: Keeps the shoulder blades flat on the support arms (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.serratus_l: Keeps the shoulder blades flat on the support arms (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.triceps_r: Keep the support elbows straight (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.triceps_l: Keep the support elbows straight (clinical opinion).
